verdict: Caution: lend selectively to branded, fire-compliant plywood and laminate units with verified timber sourcing; avoid unbranded commodity plywood and any unit with unresolved fire-safety or stock-insurance gaps.
title: Kandla-Gandhidham plywood, veneer & laminates: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**Plywood is timber converted into glued boards; cash turns on veneer availability, drying, pressing and working-capital discipline.** Face veneer, core timber and chemicals are the key inputs, and plants located near raw material do better on cost [8]. Kandla matters because it is a port-led cluster: CPIL runs a Kandla unit alongside Joka, Guwahati, Chennai, Karnal and Roorkee [7]. **The cluster's edge is import-linked timber and export access, which also means FX exposure** — rating commentary flags sizeable raw-material imports and product exports, partly hedged [9]. ## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in branded, value-added grades; commodity plywood is fragmented and price-competed** [6]. Peer results show the split: Greenlam's plywood segment grew 90.7% YoY with gross margin at 55.0% but EBITDA margin at 10.6% [2], and later plywood-incl-veneer revenue rose 22.2% YoY [4]. **So when a proposal lands, check the product mix — branded laminate and value-added board versus plain commercial plywood; if the mix is commodity, ask for the price-realisation trend and customer concentration.**

## What has changed now
**A fire at a Kabrau plywood company gutted machinery and stock, drawing firefighters from Bhachau, Kandla and Gandhidham** [1]. **So on every site visit, check fire NOC, hydrant and stock-insurance cover; if machinery or stock is uninsured or the NOC is expired, ask for remediation before sanction.** Nationally, IIP for NIC 16 is +8.6% YoY but -0.8% Apr-to-date, while bank credit is +20.6% YoY [D] — **so when a proposal lands, check whether growth is funded by real output or by borrowing; if credit drawdown outpaces sales, ask why.** Gujarat GST is +11.9% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], a genuine local tailwind. ## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue branded laminate and value-added plywood makers with own or contracted timber linkage, and units supplying formal builders and export buyers.** Peer guidance of 18-20% FY27 revenue growth with chemical and resin cost inflation passed on [5] supports this. **Structure as cash-flow-backed working-capital lines with stock and book-debt hypothecation; take monthly stock statements, insurance endorsements and GST returns.** Avoid unbranded commodity plywood units with thin margins and no fire cover [6]. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch veneer and chemical cost pass-through, export volume and FX.** Greenlam's laminate volume fell 7% YoY on weak exports even as revenue grew 18% [3] — **so if a borrower's volumes fall while revenue rises, ask whether price or mix is carrying it.** Chemical cost is flagged as a key margin risk [3][5].
watch: Stock cover below drawing power or lapsed policy -> freeze further drawdown
GST turnover trails bank credits by a widening gap -> ask for reconciliation
Expired NOC or no hydrant -> require remediation before renewal
Volume fall with revenue rise, or chemical cost spike not passed on -> reprice or trim limit
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local plywood-unit fire destroyed machinery and stock; cluster fire-safety and insurance risk elevated.
